title: Christ received grace for grace, and so may his followers
setting: Joseph Smith dictated this revelation in Kirtland, Ohio, on 6 May 1833, and few sources describe its background. Part of it is addressed to Frederick G. Williams, Sidney Rigdon, and Newel K. Whitney. Whitney’s note on his copy called it a reprimand about their families, though most of the text concerns the Father and the Son. Its opening echoes John 1, but the JSP judges it separate from the New Testament revision finished in February 1833.
summary: The revelation promises that those who forsake sin and obey will see Christ’s face and know that he is. It then quotes a record of John, who saw that Christ “received not of the fulness at first”. Christ continued “from grace to grace” until he received a fulness of the Father’s glory. Those who keep the commandments may also receive grace for grace and come to the Father’s fulness. The revelation says people were with God in the beginning, and that intelligence was not created. It defines truth as knowledge of things as they are, were, and will be, and calls God’s glory “light and truth”. Williams and Rigdon are rebuked for not teaching their children, and Joseph Smith and Whitney must set their families in order. Rigdon is to go on his journey and preach, and Joseph and Williams are to make haste also. All are to hasten the translation and study history and law.

contextNote.title: Grace for grace as a pattern of growth
contextNote.text: Verse 19 names the need the revelation answers: to “know how to worship, and know what you worship”. Verses 12–13 answer by describing how Christ himself grew. He “received not of the fulness at first” but “continued from grace to grace”. Verse 20 applies the same pattern to the hearers: keep the commandments, and “you shall receive grace for grace”. Verse 28 restates it as receiving truth and light until one “knoweth all things”. In this passage, grace for grace names gradual growth, step by step, toward the Father’s fulness.

ldsText: The 2025 Come, Follow Me lesson for section 93, “Receive of His Fulness,” teaches that we can grow as the Savior did. According to verses 12–20 and 28, what moves a person from one degree of grace to the next?
reviewNote: Read all 53 verses. Official heading gives only Kirtland, 6 May 1833. JSP introduction read for the sparse sources, Whitney’s docket, the parallels with John 1, and its distance from the completed Bible revision. The John of verses 6–18 is not identified in the text (readers differ between the Apostle and the Baptist), so no person id is added. The purpose of Rigdon’s journey in verse 51 was not confirmed. Fact-check 2026-10-12: setting said the Bible revision was finished in February; JSP says the New Testament revision was finished 2 February 1833 (whole Bible not until July). Corrected. Fact-check 2026-10-12: summary said Joseph and Williams were sent to travel and preach; verse 52 only tells them to “make haste also” (verse 51 sends Rigdon to preach). Corrected.
